title: Getting jobs, pay and places played
summary: Engagements came by cards and phone at $2.75 a man for four hours; he lists Storyville cabarets, hotels and out-of-town towns.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: tell us about the various jobs that you played, how you got them, and how you made arrangements for them?

Well, I'll tell you, the, the leader of the band usually have cards made, and, and a phone number. So naturally, when they want you, they phone you, that, uh, they got an engagement for you. Then the price is as usual, $2.75 a man. That's what you got in the night, but four hours work, from eight to 12.
Mr. Dewey, would you tell us the various place, places that your band played while you were in New Orleans?

Mr. Dewey, would you tell us the, uh, the band played? Among, among the, among the players, there's the 101 Wrench, uh, Pete Lawless Cabaret, and Nagel and Vor, Nagel and Hunt's Cabaret. There's three places right there, in the Storyville. Now, but I played at, uh, uh, Cardinal. Yeah, I played in the Blue Room, Roosevelt Hotel with A.J. Piron. I played at, uh, Racetrack. I played at Franchina. I played at, uh, West End. What about the Montelion? Montelion Hotel Blue Room. I also played, uh, that's right, go right ahead. I started at, I even played at Millenburg, and Old Lady Lee, both, both of the questions from New Orleans to Covington.
Oh. Uh, Mr. Dewey, did you play in other places outside of New Orleans, Mississippi, etc.? Do you recall any places that you played? Yeah, with some, someone else. I was only hired.
